what_it_does: Sparse neural networks skip many multiplications, which should make them faster — but irregular, unpredictable memory-access patterns cause the chip's internal fast memory (cache) to miss frequently, stalling the processor while it waits for data from slower main memory. NVR borrows an idea called 'runahead execution': a lightweight background thread runs ahead of the main computation, guesses which memory addresses will be needed soon, and fetches them early so the data is already waiting when the main thread arrives. The key claim is that this prefetching mechanism requires less than 5% extra chip area and works without any changes to the software compiler.
